program.teacherCertification: Refer to the Course Structure section.
program.purpose: This program offers a sequence of courses that provides coherent and rigorous content aligned with challenging academic standards and relevant technical knowledge and skills needed to prepare for further education and careers in the Government & Public Administration career cluster; provides technical skill proficiency, and includes competency-based applied learning that contributes to the academic knowledge, higher-order reasoning and problem-solving skills, work attitudes, general employability skills, technical skills, and occupation-specific skills, and knowledge of all aspects of the Government & Public Administration career cluster.
program.programStructure: This program is a planned sequence of instruction consisting of two credits. To teach the course(s) listed below, instructors must hold at least one of the teacher certifications indicated for that course.

alternates.note: The Public Service Research requirement may be fulfilled by completing Advanced Placement Research, provided that the student's final course project focuses on a public service issue.

additionalInformation.heading: Laboratory Activities
additionalInformation.body: Laboratory investigations that include scientific inquiry, research, measurement, problem solving, emerging technologies, tools and equipment, as well as, experimental, quality, and safety procedures are an integral part of this career and technical program/course. Laboratory investigations benefit all students by developing an understanding of the complexity and ambiguity of empirical work, as well as the skills required to manage, operate, calibrate and troubleshoot equipment/tools used to make observations. Students understand measurement error; and have the skills to aggregate, interpret, and present the resulting data. Equipment and supplies should be provided to enhance hands-on experiences for students.

additionalInformation.heading: Florida Standards for English Language Development (ELD)
additionalInformation.body: English language learners communicate for social and instructional purposes within the school setting. ELD.K12.ELL.SI.1 -- Teachers are required to provide listening, speaking, reading and writing instruction that allows English language learners (ELL) to communicate for social and instructional purposes within the school setting. For the given level of English language proficiency and with visual, graphic, or interactive support, students will interact with grade level words, expressions, sentences and discourse to process or produce language necessary for academic success. The ELD standard should specify a relevant content area concept or topic of study chosen by curriculum developers and teachers which maximizes an ELL's need for communication and social skills. For additional information on the development and implementation of the ELD standards, please contact the Bureau of Student Achievement through Language Acquisition at sala@fldoe.org.

additionalInformation.heading: Career and Technical Student Organization (CTSO)
additionalInformation.body: CTSOs are co-curricular career and technical student organizations providing leadership training and reinforcing specific career and technical skills. Career and Technical Student Organizations provide activities for students as an integral part of the instruction offered. Other CTSOs not listed in this curriculum framework or recognized by the Florida Department of Education are permissible provided they support student mastery over the standards and benchmarks of this curriculum framework.

additionalInformation.heading: Cooperative Training - OJT
additionalInformation.body: On-the-job training is appropriate but not required for this program. Whenever offered, the rules, guidelines, and requirements specified in the OJT framework apply.

additionalInformation.heading: Accommodations
additionalInformation.body: Federal and state legislation requires the provision of accommodations for students with disabilities as identified on the secondary student's Individual Educational Plan (IEP) or 504 plan or postsecondary student's accommodations' plan to meet individual needs and ensure equal access. Accommodations change the way the student is instructed. Students with disabilities may need accommodations in such areas as instructional methods and materials, assignments and assessments, time demands and schedules, learning environment, assistive technology and special communication systems. Documentation of the accommodations requested and provided should be maintained in a confidential file. In addition to accommodations, some secondary students with disabilities (students with an IEP served in Exceptional Student Education (ESE)) will need modifications to meet their needs. Modifications change the outcomes or what the student is expected to learn, e.g., modifying the curriculum of a secondary career and technical education course. Note: postsecondary curriculum and regulated secondary programs cannot be modified. Some secondary students with disabilities (ESE) may need additional time (i.e., longer than the regular school year), to master the student performance standards associated with a regular course or a modified course. If needed, a student may enroll in the same career and technical course more than once. Documentation should be included in the IEP that clearly indicates that it is anticipated that the student may need an additional year to complete a Career and Technical Education (CTE) course. The student should work on different competencies and new applications of competencies each year toward completion of the CTE course. After achieving the competencies identified for the year, the student earns credit for the course. It is important to ensure that credits earned by students are reported accurately. The district's information system must be designed to accept multiple credits for the same course number for eligible students with disabilities.

courses.title: Public Service Research
courses.description: The course is designed to develop competencies in research focusing on public service. Students will demonstrate critical thinking and academic research skills on a public service topic. It is strongly encouraged that students will select a public service topic about which they focused in their experiential learning course. Students who have completed AP Seminar may select AP Research as an alternate to "Research in Public Service" to complete the "Research in Public Service" curricular requirement. Students completing AP Research to replace the "Research in Public Service" curricular requirement must focus their research on a public service issue or topic to count AP Research toward their Public Service Career Pathway requirements.

standards.courseTitle: Public Service Research
standards.text: Communicate through writing.

benchmarks.text: Develop written documents using computer-based word processing in a proficient manner.

Write to argue a position, supporting claims using logical reasoning and credible evidence from multiple sources, rebutting counterclaims with relevant evidence, using a logical organizational structure, elaboration, purposeful transitions, and maintaining a formal and objective tone.
Write expository texts to explain and analyze information from multiple sources, using a logical organization, purposeful transitions, and a tone and voice appropriate to the task.
Improve writing by considering feedback from adults, peers, and/or online editing tools, revising to address the needs of a specific audience.

Compare the development of two opposing arguments on the same topic, evaluating the effectiveness and validity of the claims, and analyzing the ways in which the authors use the same information to achieve different ends.

threads.label: Public service leadership
threads.rationale: Leadership traits, then the civic dispositions behind public service, then leading a group to a goal, then the expertise and active practice that make it real.

threads.label: Origins and purposes of government
threads.rationale: The same founding-documents standard is required in all four courses; teach it once in Leadership, then deepen it rather than restart it.

threads.label: Citizenship and civic participation
threads.rationale: Roles, rights and responsibilities of citizens recur in every course, growing from explanation toward evaluation and advocacy.

threads.label: Structure and functions of government
threads.rationale: The branches, federalism and regulatory agencies repeat across all four courses; Leadership carries the fullest treatment.

threads.label: World affairs and foreign policy
threads.rationale: Foreign policy builds directly on the origins-of-government work in the same course.

threads.label: Communication and debate
threads.rationale: Interpersonal skills, then ELA expectations, then genre and technique, then the Florida Civics and Debate Initiative, then formal oral presentation of research.

threads.label: Argument and analysis in writing
threads.rationale: Argumentative writing and informational analysis in Communication become the research writing and ELA expectations of the capstone.

threads.label: Research practice
threads.rationale: Research to answer a question, first in Communication, then as the full investigative project in Public Service Research.

threads.label: Technology and work products
threads.rationale: Word processing, slides and spreadsheets recur in every course; each pass should raise the standard of the product, not reteach the tool.

threads.label: Problem solving and decision making
threads.rationale: Public leadership information gathering, then a decision-making model applied to a community policy issue, then project-management problem-solving tools.

threads.label: Project management foundations
threads.rationale: Terminology, then planning concepts, roles, tools and plan-based approaches, ending in the schedule.

threads.label: Running a project
threads.rationale: Implementation, situation classification, plan attributes, team roles and document controls - the work between the plan and the deliverable.

threads.label: Stakeholders and closeout
threads.rationale: Frameworks and stakeholder communication, information gathering, milestones, and finally the completed deliverable.

topics.label: Leadership
activities: Interview or host a public servant, then map their decisions against leadership styles studied

topics.label: Civic Dispositions
materials: Excerpts from the Declaration of Independence and Federalist Papers
activities: Structured seminar on a founding text, with students taking and defending evidence-based positions

topics.label: Founding Documents
activities: Trace one political principle (checks and balances, federalism) from a founding text to a current news story

topics.label: Structure of Government
activities: Map a single policy from proposal to enactment to enforcement across all three branches

topics.label: State and Local Government
activities: Attend or stream a local commission meeting and brief the class on one agenda item

topics.label: Elections and Public Policy
activities: Track one bill or ballot measure and chart who is trying to influence it and how

topics.label: Media Literacy
materials: Paired news coverage of one event
activities: Evaluate two accounts of the same event for bias, omission and emotional appeal

topics.label: Foreign Policy and World Affairs
materials: Map of treaty and alliance relationships
activities: Position paper on a current foreign policy decision, argued from stated national interests

topics.label: Communication and Debate
materials: Florida Civics and Debate Initiative materials
activities: Run a formal debate round, then have speakers self-assess from the recording

topics.label: Writing and Argument
activities: Write an argument on a public issue, then revise it after a structured peer review

topics.label: Reading and Text Analysis
activities: Compare two opposing arguments on one topic and judge which uses its evidence better

topics.label: Research
activities: Narrow a public-service question, gather sources, and defend the findings in a presentation

topics.label: Project Management
activities: Charter a real class or school project: scope it, schedule it, assign roles, then run it

topics.label: Project Roles and Teams
activities: Assign and rotate project roles across a term so every student leads once

topics.label: Monitoring and Controls
activities: Run a weekly status check against the plan and log what changed and why

topics.label: Problem Solving and Decision Making
activities: Apply a decision-making model to a real community issue and defend the alternative chosen

topics.label: Meetings and Facilitation
activities: Each student chairs one working meeting with an agenda, minutes and action items

topics.label: Information Gathering
activities: Gather information on one issue from three different source types and reconcile the differences

topics.label: Technology and Work Products
materials: Word processor, slides and spreadsheet software
activities: Produce the same findings as a written brief, a slide deck and a data table, then compare which lands

topics.label: Ethics and Professionalism
activities: Judge a real public-service ethics case against a published code of conduct

topics.label: Employability and Job Attainment
activities: Apply to a real posted position end to end: resume, cover letter, portfolio, mock interview

topics.label: Career and Academic Planning
activities: Build a personal plan comparing two postsecondary pathways on cost, debt and placement

topics.label: Experiential Learning
activities: Place students with a local agency and require a structured reflection against the standards

topics.label: Economics and Public Finance
activities: Trace one line item in a public budget from proposal to approval

topics.label: Working Across Difference
activities: Group task that deliberately mixes perspectives, with a debrief on how difference changed the outcome

topics.label: Career Readiness Skills
activities: Self-assess against the employability rubric at the start and end of the term

notes.detail: The program-structure table names course 8918050 "Public Service Officer"; the Student Performance Standards page for the same course number names it "Police Service Officer". Both titles are retained (title / altTitle).
Standards 28.0+ are re-used by all three fourth-credit options (8918050, 8918060, 8918070). A benchmark number such as 28.01 is only unique when paired with its course number.

Benchmark text is transcribed verbatim, including source typos (e.g. 33.11 "Determining how the crash occurred.", 36.01 stray list marker "q) restitution", 42.05 "the circumstances and officer must consider").

Instructional threads, prerequisites and the canonical program order come from data/pathways.json (curated) plus the framework's own numbering. They are a teaching judgement, not an FLDOE mandate - edit the file and rebuild to change how sequences are generated.
cognitiveLevel, modality, topics, weight and suggestedPeriods are derived heuristics for planning support - they are not part of the FLDOE framework.
